description.narrative:
Water cooperation for inclusive and participatory river restoration
Building on the Twinning Agreement between Bangladesh and the Netherlands and supporting the implementation of the UNECE Water Convention, IHE Delft Institute for Water Education proposes a tailor-made capacity-strengthening programme that directly supports inclusive riverbed restoration and livelihood development. The training contributes to the implementation of the Convention by equipping local communities and authorities with the knowledge and cooperative skills required for inclusive, participatory, and ecosystem-focused water governance at the basin level. The Programme is intended for representatives of local communities, local authorities, civil society organisations, and water user groups engaged in the restoration process, with particular encouragement for the participation of women, youth, and marginalised groups. It is designed tobuild participants’ knowledge, skills, and confidence so they can engage effectively in planning, dialogue, and decision-making. Bycombining thematic expertise with practical, participatory methods, the Programme will help ensure that the project’s planning process is grounded in inclusive, well-informed, and cooperative approaches to water management.
Goals of the training The training will contribute directly to the project’s participatory planning process by: Strengthening stakeholder capacities for inclusive and cooperative river restoration. Equipping local communities and authorities with foundational knowledge in water governance, hydrology, environmental planning, and climate adaptation so they can engage confidently and constructively in the planning process. Enhancing understanding of the link between local actions and basin-wide cooperation. Highlighting how community-level decisions, ecosystem health, and local governance interact with national and transboundary water cooperation under the UNECE Water Convention framework. Providing analytical tools and global experiences relevant to the Bangladesh context. Introducing practical case studies and lessons from comparable river restoration and community-engagement initiatives worldwide to inspire locally adapted solutions and broaden participants’ perspective on possibilities. Supporting informed participation and dialogue throughout the Planning Process. Building practical skills in collaboration and conflict-sensitive water cooperation so that local actors are prepared to contribute to multi-stakeholder discussions and co-create restoration strategies. These goals directly reinforce the project’s central ambition: a participatory, knowledge-informed, and socially inclusive river restoration process that strengthens cooperation at both local and broader governance levels. Format The Programme will start in February 2026 and will run until September 2026. The Programme follows a hybrid format combining online learning, in-person engagement, and collaborative assignments, which will be designed based on the pre-training needs assessment and in alignment with the Participatory Planning Process . A hybrid design enables regular engagement over several months while minimising travel burdens, ensuring flexibility for community members and local officials, and allowing learningto remain closely aligned with the evolving participatory planning process. Elements of the Programme include the following: 1. Optional: A short Pre-Training Needs Assessment (Feb 2026) will be conducted to ensure that all modules, examples, and exercises are tailored to the specific capacities, knowledge levels, and priorities of participants. 2. 10 thematic online lectures and discussion (Mar – Aug 2026), every 2-3 weeks. The duration: 2.5h each in the afternoon in Bangladesh / morning in the Netherlands. 3. Preparatory readings (1–2 short pieces) to support knowledge building before each session. 4. Individual assignments: participants will be asked to work individually on their own task, which will later be presented and discussed with a larger group. 5. Group assignments, aligned with the Participatory Planning Process, to encourage collective problem-solving. 6. In-person training: Four days of interactive workshops in Bangladesh focusing on foundational knowledge about water conflicts and cooperation, practical training, including collaborative methods and tools. 7. Simulated role-play exercise on transboundary water cooperation to strengthen systems thinking, negotiation practice, and cooperative problem solving. Content The Programme’s content will remain closely aligned with the evolvingParticipatory Planning Process. The topics below form a provisional outline and may be adjusted in consultation with project partners and based on pre-training needs assessment to ensure relevance. Topics for online lectures can include the following topics: - Introduction to water governance and cooperation - Introduction to hydrology - Water management and environmental planning in the delta - Drinking water security - Local adaptation for climate resilience - Groundwater - Wastewater and desalination - Integrated waterresources management - Institutions for water management in Bangladesh - Community-based water governance
In-person trainings topics: - Water conflict and cooperation - International Water Law - Institutions for transboundary water cooperation - Water diplomacy - Inclusivity and participation - Roleplay on transboundary water cooperation The final list of thematic lectures for both online lectures and in-person trainings will be defined based on pre-training needs assessment and/or in consultations with Oxfam Bangladesh.

participating-org.narrative: IHE Delft Institute for Water Educa

Water poses a serious challenge to every part of the world. Too many people remain without access to water and sanitation. This makes their lives difficult: their health suffers and prosperity remains out of reach. Increasingly frequent and severe droughts and floods - a result of climate change - add to the challenge. At IHE Delft Institute for Water Education, we work to change this. Our vision: a world free of poverty and injustice in which people manage their water and environmental resources sustainably and equitably Education, research and capacity development We address water and sanitation challenges through education, research and capacity development, at global, national, local and even microscopic scales – the latter in our laboratories. We focus on all water-related fields, including social sciences, engineering and more. Our world-class experts teach and research fields such as climate change adaptation, governance, water diplomacy, desalination, water supply, wetlands and sustainable hydropower. Together with Dutch and international partners, we offer high-quality education, including an MSc Programme in Water and Sustainable Development, a PhD programme,diploma courses, various short courses and online courses as well as customized training and capacity development, all within a uniquely international and interdisciplinary environment. People seeking to make an impact for water and environment, including water professionals, scientists, engineers, practitioners, consultants, activists,decision-makers, change-makers and others, come to IHE Delft to sharpen their ability to contribute to global sustainable development.
